questions.q: Where would you look first to find a query consuming disproportionate CPU on a SQL Server instance?
options: sys.dm_exec_requests, sorted by CPU time
sys.change_tracking_tables
sys.extended_properties
The Windows Event Viewer Application log only
questions.explain: sys.dm_exec_requests shows active requests and their resource consumption, including CPU time, letting you identify the offending session.

questions.q: Why is tempdb filling up especially disruptive compared to a single database filling up?
options: Tempdb is shared across the entire instance, so new work everywhere can start failing, not just the query that caused the pressure
Tempdb cannot be monitored with any DMV
Filling tempdb only affects Reporting Services
Tempdb has no effect on ordinary query execution
questions.explain: Tempdb backs sorts, hashes, row versioning, and temp objects for the whole instance, so exhausting it has instance-wide impact.

Log backups have never been configured for this database
The database is in simple recovery model
Tempdb is full
questions.explain: ACTIVE_TRANSACTION specifically means an open transaction is holding back log truncation — running a log backup alone won't fix it until that transaction ends.

questions.q: What is the best practice for handling disk space exhaustion, per this lesson?
options: Catch it before it happens with disk-space alerting, since a surprise full drive is almost always preventable
Ignore it since SQL Server automatically compresses data when a drive fills
Always restore from backup as the first response
Disable the transaction log to prevent drives from filling
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that disk exhaustion is usually fixable fast once discovered, but the real value is proactive alerting so it isn't a surprise.

questions.q: In a blocking chain of several sessions, where should stabilization efforts focus?
options: The head of the chain — the one session actually holding the lock everyone else is waiting on
The last session in the chain, since it has waited the longest
Every session equally, killed simultaneously
Only sessions with the highest CPU usage, regardless of blocking status
questions.explain: Addressing the session actually holding the lock (the head of the chain) resolves the blocking for everyone waiting behind it.
